ask: C11, POSIX. progress.c: reusable ANSI progress bar — determinate and indeterminate modes, throughput and ETA estimation with exponential smoothing, terminal width detection via ioctl, carriage-return redraw, and a demo loop over 200 items. write the file.
prose:
`progress.c` written — 11 KB, compiles clean with:

```
cc -std=c11 -Wall -Wextra -o progress progress.c
./progress
```

A few design notes worth calling out:

**Smoothing (α = 0.15).** Lower than the typical 0.2 so the ETA doesn't thrash on bursty workloads. Tune `PROGRESS_SMOOTH_ALPHA` upward if you want the displayed rate to track changes faster.

**Layout math.** The bar width is computed fresh every redraw from `ioctl(TIOCGWINSZ)`, so it adapts if the user resizes the terminal mid-run. Minimum inner width is clamped at 4 so the bar never disappears on narrow outputs.

**Indeterminate slider.** Width is 1/8 of the bar (min 3), bouncing one column per `progress_update` call. If you're calling it faster than ~30 Hz you may want to gate advancement on a minimum elapsed time rather than call count.

**Thread safety.** Not present — `progress_t` is single-owner. If you're updating from worker threads, wrap `progress_update` in a mutex or accumulate deltas atomically and have a single render thread call in.

The `progress_init` / `progress_update` / `progress_finish` trio is the full public surface — drop `progress_t` on the stack, call the three functions, done.
